item.title: Skills event in Shanghai showcases young talent
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Skills event in Shanghai showcases young talent President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the 48th World-Skills Competition, which opened on Tuesday in Shanghai, highlighting that sweeping technological and industrial changes are reshaping global vocational skill development and reaffirming China's commitment to cultivating young skilled talent. In the letter, Xi said China stands ready to deepen exchanges and cooperation with all participating parties to advance global skills development, better contribute to world economic growth and improve people's livelihoods and well-being. Xi said the new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is accelerating, bringing profound and far-reaching changes to global vocational skills development. The WorldSkills Competition closely aligns with industry needs and provides a valuable platform for skilled professionals from around the world to hone their skills and learn from and exchange experiences with one another, Xi said. China will inspire and guide more workers, especially young people, to achieve career success through professional skills, he said. Premier Li Qiang attended the event and officially declared the competition open. Before the opening ceremony, Li met with WorldSkills International President Francis Hourant and Chief Executive Officer David Hoey. The ceremony was held at the Shanghai World Expo Cultural Center and began with a colorful and energetic parade featuring skilled young competitors from around the world. Delegations marched along the "Skill Dream Avenue", an indoor-outdoor thoroughfare, greeting spectators at an outdoor plaza before proceeding into the venue. Live performances celebrated China's rich craft heritage, combining reenactments of the use of ancient Chinese skills with multimedia renderings of the Silk Road to connect local and global skills traditions. Humanoid robots performed alongside human artists, underscoring the role of human creativity in driving technological progress. During the event, skilled young workers from different continents shared their own experiences, highlighting how vocational skills can transform lives. A total of 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions will compete in Shanghai from Wednesday through Saturday at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai). The closing ceremony will be held on Sunday. China's 71 competitors, with an average age of 21, are competing in all 64 skills, highlighting the country's pool of young skilled talent. Since China's debut at the 2011 WorldSkills Competition in London, Chinese competitors have won 93 gold medals and topped both the gold medal table and the overall team rankings at four consecutive WorldSkills editions. At a news conference before the ceremony, Zhai Tao, deputy director of the department of vocational capacity building at the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, said China joined WorldSkills International in 2010 as its 53rd member. In the years since, the organization has expanded to a network of 90 member countries and regions, reflecting the growing recognition of skills development worldwide, Zhai said. Wang Di, director of the WorldSkills Competition China (Shanghai) Research Center, said the WorldSkills Competition is not merely about technology, but is closely linked to clearly defined occupations.

item.title: Greenland deal inked at UN gathering
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Greenland deal inked at UN gathering Denmark, Greenland, and the United States inked a deal on Tuesday that observers say is aimed at appeasing the US side, after months of threats and posturing. The current US administration has repeatedly coveted the strategically located and mineral-rich island of Greenland, despite it belonging to fellow NATO member Denmark, and the US president has even refused to rule out using military or economic force to secure it. Now, after lengthy negotiations, the three parties have reached an agreement that will allow the US to have a larger military presence on the island, and access to its vast energy resources. Reuters said its sources reported Washington is planning to open two new military sites on the massive, sparsely-populated island as a result — at Narsarsuaq, a former Cold War airbase, and at Mestersvig. The new bases will complement the sole current US presence in Greenland, at the Pituffik Space Base. US President Donald Trump, Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen inked the agreement at a trilateral signing ceremony at the UN General Assembly in the US city of New York on Tuesday. Frederiksen told Danish radio DR: "It is a good agreement from a Danish point of view. And when it benefits the Nordic countries and security in the Arctic region, it also benefits NATO and Europe." Denmark's Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said the deal means Arctic security will now be NATO's collective responsibility. He told national broadcaster TV2: "It will be in a form where responsibility for security in the Arctic is not only Danish or American." Denmark added that the agreement also ensures its continued sovereignty over Greenland, and guarantees Greenland's continued right to devolved self-government. Trump expressed a different interpretation on social media, saying the deal means the US will have "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland". AFP reported that the deal is aimed at ensuring the US has exclusive access to Greenland's strategic and physical resources, and that other countries are excluded. Washington has been interested in Greenland since at least World War II, when the US signed a 1941 deal with a Danish envoy to protect the island at a time when Denmark was occupied by German forces. The US tried to follow that up in 1946 by purchasing the island, but Copenhagen declined to sell. However, Washington and Copenhagen inked a deal in 1951 that gave the US extensive rights to locate military assets in Greenland, under the supervision of the NATO military alliance. That agreement led to the US establishing 17 military sites on Greenland and stationing more than 10,000 personnel there. Currently, Pituffik Space Base is the only active US base on the island, and is home to around 150 US military personnel.

item.title: More influential US families focus on learning Chinese
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
More influential US families focus on learning Chinese Billionaires in the United States are encouraging their children to learn Chinese as China's influence grows on the world stage, language experts said. The country's elite, including the world's richest person, Elon Musk, as well as US President Donald Trump, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, are reportedly eager for their offspring to learn Mandarin, according to multiple reports and their own admissions. Musk, 55, tweeted in Chinese on May 14: "My son is currently learning Mandarin." He posted the tweet after he was asked by a commentator on social media platform X why he had taken his 6-year-old son on a trip to China for Trump and President Xi Jinping's summit in Beijing in May. Musk accompanied Trump on the trip, along with former Apple CEO Tim Cook, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other US businesspeople. During the visit, Musk's son was seen wearing a neo-Chinese style embroidered top and carrying a traditional tiger-head bag at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Experts suggested that US elites want their children to learn Chinese due to the links and opportunities connected to the world's second-largest economy. "My guess is many people think that being able to speak Mandarin will lead to more job opportunities in the future," Seth Wiener, an associate professor and director of graduate studies in the Department of Languages, Cultures and Applied Linguistics at Carnegie Mellon University, told China Daily. "Learning Mandarin, or any new language, has many benefits. These include increased professional and social opportunities, access to new culture and media, and a broader perspective on the world," he said. Mandarin is the official language of China, while Cantonese is widely spoken in southern China, mostly in Guangdong province. As for Trump's grandchildren, two have already demonstrated their Mandarin skills. During the April 2017 visit by Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to Mara-Lago in the US state of Florida, Trump's 5-year-old granddaughter Arabella Kushner and her younger brother Joseph sang the traditional Chinese folk song Jasmine Flower in Chinese, and recited the Three-Character Classic, a traditional text from the 13th century. Arabella also recited Tang Dynasty (618-907) poetry by Li Bai. "Very proud of Arabella and Joseph for their performance in honor of President Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan's official visit to the US!" the children's mother, Ivanka Trump, tweeted on April 7, 2017. Arabella's Mandarin language skills were also on display during Chinese New Year in February 2017, when Ivanka Trump shared a video on social media of Arabella singing a Happy New Year song in Mandarin. Trump showed Xi a video of Arabella singing and reciting Mandarin poetry during their afternoon tea at the Forbidden City and later at a banquet at the Great Hall of the People in November 2017, the Associated Press reported. According to US tech media outlet Business Insider, Ivanka Trump and her husband, Jared Kushner, have three children and have reportedly hired a Mandarin-speaking nanny to help the children learn the language on a daily basis. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, 62, the world's fourth-richest person, with an estimated net worth of $224 billion, according to Forbes magazine, and his ex-wife MacKenzie Scott, 56, have four children. In a 2013 interview with Vogue magazine, Scott said that they had tried homeschooling their children at one point. Scott, a philanthropist with an estimated net worth of $27.8 billion, told Vogue: "We tried all sorts of things … including Mandarin lessons, the Singapore math program, and lots of clubs and sports with other neighborhood kids." Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 42, the fifth-richest person in the world with a net worth of $222 billion according to Forbes, and his wife, Priscilla Chan, have also ensured that their children are bilingual. Chan, the daughter of ethnic Chinese refugees who left Vietnam, speaks fluent Cantonese. Their daughter, Max, was seen in a video uploaded by her father on Facebook in 2016, practicing Mandarin with the help of an artificial intelligence assistant. Zuckerberg has demonstrated his own Mandarin skills by conducting a 30-minute question-and-answer session in the language. A growing number of people from Western countries are eager to learn Mandarin on TikTok and other social media sites. However, experts said that many find it complicated at first, as it differs substantially from English. "I suspect it is a more difficult language (to learn), as Americans are not as familiar with tones," Gregory H. Patton, a professor of clinical management communication at the University of Southern California's Marshall School of Business and an expert in communication and leadership effectiveness, told China Daily. Wiener from Carnegie Mellon University agreed, adding that "two of the most prominent differences are the speech sounds and the writing system". But he said it is easier for children to learn languages more quickly than adults, giving the elite's children a head start.

item.title: Global hopes for stability hinge on visit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Global hopes for stability hinge on visit Observers say high-level engagement will shore up confidence in a turbulent world President Xi Jinping's upcoming visit to the United States is garnering widespread global attention, as the high-level engagement between China and the US is expected to steer bilateral relations toward stability and shore up confidence in a turbulent world. Xi will make a state visit to the US from Wednesday to Friday, at the invitation of US President Donald Trump. This will be his second state visit to the US since 2015, and comes within six months of Trump's state visit to China in May. Observers said the exchange of visits between the heads of state of the world's two largest economies is "very significant" and "consequential" for the global economy, because steady Sino-US ties hold the key to world peace and stability. US Congresswoman Judy Chu said, "It is very significant that President Xi is coming to Washington, DC", highlighting the importance of the two leaders having "an opportunity to meet face-to-face and discuss the major issues affecting the relationship". Positive signal Edward Cai, president of the All American Chinese Association in Southern California, expressed hope that the meeting would "send positive signals regarding stabilizing relations, strengthening communication, enhancing mutual trust and expanding cooperation". "It is not alarming for differences to exist between China and the US. The key lies in maintaining dialogue, managing differences and avoiding miscalculation and confrontation," he said. Cai emphasized that the stable development of China-US relations serves not only the shared interests of the two peoples, but is also crucial for global peace, stability and prosperity. "We have full confidence in the vision of the two leaders and the leadership demonstrated by them in steering bilateral relations toward stability," he added. Wichai Kinchong Choi, senior vice-president at Kasikornbank in Thailand, said that it is "always a positive sign when the leaders of the world's two major powers sit down and talk". Emphasizing the importance of high-level dialogue "at a time when the global economy is facing tremendous uncertainty", Choi said that "constructive engagement between China and the US will not only benefit the two countries, but also provide greater certainty for businesses and economies in the (Asia-Pacific) region". Mohamed Sabreen, an expert in international affairs and Middle East issues based in Cairo, Egypt, said that "dialogue and managed competition are more constructive than confrontational policies". He also warned that "a renewed trade war or deeper strategic tensions would create uncertainty far beyond Washington and Beijing". "Middle Eastern countries want to preserve their freedom to develop partnerships with both powers, rather than face the pressure to choose between them," he added. Bali Deepak, a professor of Chinese studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University in New Delhi, India, described the upcoming meeting as "very significant", because it comes at "a particularly consequential moment in US-China relations". He noted that during Trump's visit to Beijing in May, the two leaders agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability. "I think the meeting provides an opportunity to manage — rather than resolve — the structural rivalry between the two," Deepak said, referring to the US-initiated tariffs and other pressuring tactics against China in recent years. "The US-China relationship is perhaps the single most consequential external relationship for the strategic environment of the Asia-Pacific. Greater stability between Washington and Beijing could reduce uncertainty for Asian economies and supply chains," he added. James Shikwati, founder and director of the Inter Region Economic Network, a think tank based in Nairobi, Kenya, said that "for Africa, stable relations between the US and China are preferable to confrontation", as this will yield "a predictable international environment" for the continent's development. AI-based technologies Klaus Heinrich Raditio, a lecturer in international relations at the Driyarkara School of Philosophy in Jakarta, Indonesia, said that the two countries should cooperate in developing AI-based technologies to ensure greater peace and stability. "Indonesia hopes that countries in the Global South will be involved in the development and utilization of AI-based technologies," he added. In May, Xi and Trump agreed on a new vision of building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability over the next three years and beyond. During the visit, Xi will have an in-depth exchange of views with Trump on major issues concerning bilateral relations as well as world peace and development, Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said on Monday. Yang Wanli in Bangkok, and Wang Xiaodong and Edith Mutethya in Nairobi contributed to this story.

item.title: Up close and personal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Up close and personal Face-to-face interactions and shared experiences through US youth exchanges open doorway to mutual understanding, empathy Joshua Calandrella tried acupuncture and experienced humai, a throat-singing technique from the Inner Mongolia autonomous region, for the first time during the 2026 Discover China Program hosted by Beijing Foreign Studies University in June. Both encounters offered the PhD candidate in literature and criticism at Indiana University of Pennsylvania a closer look at traditional Chinese culture. "Unlike treatments that only touch the surface, I felt the acupuncture deep inside — the qi, the inner energy, was flowing," Calandrella said. "It's completely different from taking a pill. With traditional Chinese medicine, you can feel the results immediately." It was Calandrella's second trip to China through the exchange program. This time, he joined 15 other students and professors from the United States and explored different facets of the country, from visiting the technology company Ant Group to learning about traditional Chinese culture. Their journey also took them beyond Beijing to Yiwu, Zhejiang province, where they visited the Yiwu International Trade City — the largest small commodity wholesale market in the world — gaining a glimpse into the city's vibrant commercial life, and local educational institutions. Calandrella's experience is part of a broader expansion of people-to-people exchanges between China and the US, giving more young Americans opportunities to see and experience the country firsthand. An initiative was launched in late 2023 to invite 50,000 young Americans to China for exchange and study programs over a five-year period. By May this year, more than 50,000 participants had visited China, reaching the target two and a half years ahead of schedule.

item.title: Xi's visit to boost prospects of ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Xi's visit to boost prospects of ties Scholars credit head-of-state diplomacy for cooperation gains With President Xi Jinping set to kick off his state visit to the United States on Wednesday, leading scholars from both countries expressed hope that the world's two largest economies, driven by head-of-state diplomacy, can find more areas for cooperation and shore up the prospects for improved global governance. Counting this visit and US President Donald Trump's state visit to China in May, the two countries will reach a milestone with the exchange of state visits within half a year, officials and experts said. When they met in May, Xi and Trump agreed on a new vision of building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability. Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday that China is willing to work with the US to "enrich the substance" of a China-US constructive relationship of strategic stability. China is willing to "strengthen dialogue and cooperation with the US, properly manage differences, constantly enhance the well-being of the peoples of both countries, and promote world peace, stability and prosperity", he told reporters in Beijing. Calling the current China-US relationship "very much a leader-driven relationship", Elizabeth Knup, special adviser to China Focus at The Carter Center, a US-based think tank, said both countries "need to shrink what is competitive and expand what is not competitive, and hopefully that is what is happening". "One of the most positive examples of US-China collaboration at the global level was the previous Ebola outbreak, where the US and China each brought their strength together to help address that outbreak in Africa," she said, highlighting the need for both countries to work together. In their bilateral relationship, the US and China have made some progress on the fentanyl issue, and "that continues to move forward", she said. "I hope that we can find some other areas, maybe academic exchange, where we can start to have a concrete discussion and (find) concrete ways to solve the problem," she added. Su Xiaohui, an associate research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies, said Xi's visit this week shows that China-US relations are "generally proceeding along the path of constructive strategic stability charted by the two heads of state". "Head-of-state diplomacy will once again play a strategic leading role in China-US relations. President Xi's visit to the US will serve as an important opportunity for the two heads of state to engage in strategic communication once again," she said. The international community is paying close attention to China-US head-of-state diplomacy and wants to see more promising prospects of China-US cooperation, which can offer greater certainty amid the current international situation, Su said. Earlier this year, law enforcement authorities from both countries joined hands in cracking several drug-related cases, such as a transnational case involving precursors used to manufacture synthetic cannabinoids. On Sunday, China and the US held a new round of economic and trade talks in New York. In addition to economic and trade issues and the implementation of the consensuses reached at previous rounds of talks, the two sides also discussed artificial intelligence. Su, the CIIS scholar, said that since Trump's visit to China in May, bilateral cooperation "has been more stable and improved in multiple areas". "There is strong hope that economic and trade relations will continue to serve as the ballast and driving force of China-US relations, rather than a stumbling block or source of conflict," she added. Observers said the two leaders can give a boost to global unity by advancing agendas on key common concerns. Carla Freeman, a senior lecturer for international affairs and director of the Foreign Policy Institute at Johns Hopkins University's School of Advanced International Studies, said it is a very positive factor that the two leaders have opportunities to meet. This can lead to "a more sustained, stable relationship", and "we can use this opportunity for the two leaders to meet to build more institutional arrangements" in order to help achieve that stability, she said. zhangyunbi@chinadaily.com.cn

In a recent interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Mark Greeven, professor of management innovation at the International Institute for Management Development, said, beyond competition, there is significant scope for synergy between China and the US in the field of artificial intelligence — particularly in mitigating AI risks, advancing AI for scientific discovery, and integrating software intelligence with hardware manufacturing for the real application of AI. item.title: China and US can go beyond differences
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
China and US can go beyond differences Share - WeChat
Twenty-six years ago, an American donated $5,000 to a Chinese woman he had never met. She used it to buy saplings and planted them in the sand, turning barren land into a forest. That's how the friendship began. Their reunion this August in China drew widespread attention and touched many hearts. This story demonstrates that the Chinese and American peoples share common emotions. They can transcend differences, appreciate each other, and build friendships. The hope for this relationship lies in the people.
